Baseline: self-cast ({event:'cast', from:'Hand', target:'self'}, typeLine-anchored 'Instant') and self-graveyard ({to:'Graveyard', subject:'self'}, same anchor) — both mirror Louisoix's Sacrifice's own identical baseline treatment (same Instant typeLine, same 0-7 anchor span).

The one real effect, counter ({event:'counter', target:{}, targeted:true}, oracle-anchored across the FULL two-sentence oracle text, [0,148] — both the pay-or-be-countered clause and the exile-instead-of-graveyard consequence are one continuous free-text `describe` on the single `kind:'counter'` Effect, so one combined annotation span, not two facts): reuses the exact same log-only `kind:'counter'` primitive Louisoix's Sacrifice already established — this engine has no stack/object model letting a resolving spell remove a DIFFERENT object from the stack, so there is no real target reference for `target:{}` (fully unconstrained, matching the literal 'target spell' with no type restriction at all — more permissive than Louisoix's own 'noncreature spell') to point at or move.

Two real, distinct things checked and NOT modeled, both documented in definition.ts's own long comment rather than silently dropped:
1. 'unless its controller pays {X}' — a conditional branch keyed on the COUNTERED SPELL's controller's own mid-resolution choice, not the caster's (contrast Louisoix's own 'sacrifice OR pay {2}', a real modal/ctx.mode choice the CASTER makes at cast time — a genuinely different, already-solved shape). This engine has no player-decision process anywhere (ENGINE_GAPS.md's own accepted simplification: 'every round's choices are supplied by the caller, not decided by anything in this codebase') — there is no hook for an OPPOSING player to be offered a real choice mid-resolution. `actions.counter(...)` fires unconditionally regardless, same as Louisoix's own call — not a new regression, the same log-only ceiling `kind:'counter'` already has everywhere it's used. Checked: no FIN card anywhere models a real 'unless an opponent pays' branch; Louisoix's own additional cost is the caster's own choice, a structurally different, already-solved shape, not a precedent for this one. Note: fin/79 (Swallowed by Leviathan), flagged by the task brief as a sibling card with a similar 'unless its controller pays' clause and a documented conclusion to check for consistency, does NOT exist yet in this repo (checked cards/ directory and grepped the whole pool for 'Leviathan' — no card folder, though the slug IS already pre-registered in ANNOTATED_CARD_SLUGS as a placeholder for future work) — this card's own conclusion above was reached independently, not copied from an unavailable sibling; flagged here so whoever authors fin/79 can cross-check consistency once it exists.
2. 'exile it instead of ... graveyard' — checked whether the CURRENT (2026-09-11 'Fact unification') schema, where `to`/`from` can freely co-occur with `event` on one Fact and are no longer purely-documentary `zoneFrom`/`zoneTo` fields, could represent this as real zone-matching data. Rejected: the object being exiled is a FOREIGN spell of completely unspecified type/controller (unlike Louisoix's own type-scoped 'noncreature spell'), so there is no real `subject`/`controller` this fact could honestly assert for it. Checked the pool for what a `to:'Exile'` zone-shaped fact would newly match: exactly one real zone-shaped sink wants Exile (the-darkness-crystal: `{zone:'Exile', controller:'you', types:{has:['Creature']}}`) — a TYPE- and CONTROLLER-constrained want this fact cannot honestly verify (the countered spell might not be a creature, and might belong to either player), so adding `to:'Exile'` would risk a real false-positive match, not a genuine one. Captured only as descriptive text inside `describe`, not as a new zone field — same 'don't grow the vocabulary speculatively' discipline the Constraints vocabulary itself is held to.
